models.summary: Equity defined as similarity of development levels. McKinsey logic tree picks 15 indicators in five groups. Negative indicators reversed, then min-max normalized. Entropy weights. NDI is the weighted sum. K-means splits 115 countries into High, Medium, Low. GEI is the relative gap between mean High and mean Low NDI. 2020 GEI is 14.06. EU regional check: REI falls from 2.65 in 1990 to 0.90 in 2015.
models.purpose: Score national development and measure global inequity as the gap between the top and bottom clusters.
objectives: Build a per-capita development score and a gap index that does not depend on country size.

National development level, weighted sum of normalized indicators

Same gap computed inside the EU sample

details: 115 countries, five years 2016-2020, World Bank and UNdata. Countries with too many gaps dropped.
Per capita and shares only, so country size does not enter. Cultural influence excluded.

parameter_estimation.method: Entropy weight method after reversing negative indicators. K-means with three clusters.

algorithm.description: Select 15 indicators with a logic tree, reverse cost indicators, min-max scale, entropy-weight, sum to NDI, cluster, take the relative high-low gap.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Three clusters named High, Medium, Low.

details: GEI 14.06 in 2020. High mean NDI 11249, Low mean 747. EU REI 2.65 in 1990, 0.90 in 2015. Economy 44.85 percent, civilization 25.92 percent of weight.
identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The EU decline is the only external check, and it moves in the direction the authors call logical.

strengths: The equity statistic is a gap between groups, so a large middle cannot hide the tails.
EU panel gives the index a before-and-after.
limitations: Authors reverse the usual entropy story: they say larger entropy means more significance.
K is not justified. GEI of 14 is a ratio, and the prose calls the high group hundreds of times the low group, which the table does not support (about 15 times).
missing_details: Which two EU countries switched groups.
assumptions: Omitted countries barely move the weights.
Relative and per-capita values, not totals.

models.summary: Two funding regimes, state and private, scored by fuzzy comprehensive evaluation on the same 15 factors. Evaluation grades scored 5, 2, 1, -2, -5. Membership rows are hand-set at 0.7, 0.3, and 0. State funding: IM 2.332 for more-developed countries and 2.312 for less-developed. Private funding: 2.003 and 1.708. State funding helps both more, and opens a smaller gap.
models.purpose: Compare how the funder changes the equity impact of asteroid mining.
objectives: Turn qualitative judgments about each indicator into one impact score per group and per funding regime.

variables.definition: The 15 equity indicators from the NDI model
Five grades from significant positive impact to significant negative impact
Entropy weights carried over from the NDI model
Hand-set single-factor evaluation matrix, entries 0.7, 0.3, or 0
A times R, the grade membership of one group

governing_equations.purpose: Fuzzy composition of entropy weights and the hand-set membership matrix.
Scalar impact. State: 2.332 and 2.312. Private: 2.003 and 1.708.

equation_status.note: Membership matrices (11)-(14) are badly OCR-garbled. The composition B = A·R and the four IM numbers are readable.
equation_status.reason: Numbers and the composition rule are explicit.

details: Country classes from task 1 stay fixed. Mining is a high-threshold international project, not a single-government project.
No sudden change. Individuals and small firms cannot enter.

parameter_estimation.method: Membership degrees are assigned by the authors, not estimated. 0.7, 0.3, and 0 are stipulated.

algorithm.description: Reuse the entropy weights, write a membership row per indicator for each of four cases, multiply, score, compare the four impact values.

details: IM1 2.332, IM2 2.312, IM3 2.003, IM4 1.708. State gap is smaller than the private gap.
identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The direction matches the narrative. The magnitudes are only as strong as the hand-set 0.7 and 0.3.

strengths: One number per regime makes the comparison readable.
The same weights serve both models, so the impact score is in the equity model's units.
limitations: The phrase 'very likely' is used for both 0.7 and 0.3.
Several indicator judgments are copied verbatim between the two regimes.
missing_details: Who assigned the memberships, and any agreement check.
Clean copies of matrices R1 to R4.
assumptions: Classes do not change after mining begins.
